title: Median differences between catch and detection latitude trends were not clear in four US trawl samples in 1982-2019
abstract: We tested whether catch weight and detection give different latitude trends for marine taxa. We used public trawl records from the eastern Bering Sea and Northeast US fall surveys in 1982-2019. We held survey strata, area weights, stratum positions and regional taxon sets fixed. We compared two periods for 59 Bering Sea taxa and 62 Northeast taxa. Median paired differences ranged from -4.76 to +3.74 km per decade. All four adjusted block bootstrap intervals included zero. Trend signs differed for 11 to 21 taxa per sample. An exact identity links the annual centroid gap to the spatial pattern of catch per detection. The results do not show that the two measures are equal. Detection error, catchability, survey changes, selected taxa and short time series limit inference. We measure no climate or pollution effect. The package gives code, data summaries, source hashes, checks and a figure.

display.caption: Catch weight and detection latitude trends in two regions and two periods. The right panel gives median paired differences with adjusted intervals. All four intervals include zero.
